answer: A basalt quarry guards an agent economy with a rarity ladder of violet marble: every new identity must present one marble of the tier matching its place, and each tier is ten times rarer than the last, so the first fake sifts 10 tonnes, the second 100, the third 1,000, the tenth 10 billion and the twentieth 100 quintillion tonnes, twenty fakes together 111 quintillion. Bulk farming fails because one quarry yields one marble per tier and one crew sifts, so no marble can be bought or found in parallel, like a beachcomber hunting one violet shell among pebbles, each next ten times rarer.
